items.title: Finite presentation relative to a base ring can be glued along a finite cover by principal opens
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a finite type ring map R -> A, an A-module M, and elements f_1, ..., f_r of A generating the unit ideal, and asserts the equivalence of two conditions: that each localization M_{f_i} be finitely presented relative to R, and that M itself be finitely presented relative to R (source lines 21130-21139). One implication is the localize-relative-finite-presentation lemma. For the converse, the proof writes 1 = sum f_i g_i in A and chooses a surjection from a polynomial ring in the x's and two sets of y's and z's onto A mapping y_i to f_i and z_i to g_i; this yields a surjection P = R[x, y, z]/(sum y_i z_i - 1) -> A with P a finitely presented R-algebra (proof lines 21141-21153). By the relatively-finitely-presented lemma each M_{f_i} is a finitely presented A_{f_i}-module, so by the cover criterion M is a finitely presented A-module, hence a finite P-module (proof lines 21154-21159). The substantive part is the verification that the kernel K of a surjection P^{oplus t} -> M is finite: since P_{y_i} surjects onto A_{f_i}, the lemmas cited show that each localization K_{y_i} is a finitely generated P_{y_i}-module; the proof chooses finitely many elements k_{i,j} of K generating all these localizations, lets K' be the P-submodule they generate, and concludes that K/K' has all localizations at the y_i equal to zero, whence K/K' = 0 because the y_i generate the unit ideal of P (proof lines 21160-21174). The non-routine content is the introduction of the auxiliary algebra P, which encodes the cover generators and their unit relation, and the final vanishing argument.
